_meta: BRICS/G.4 — full research dispatch, Brazil + China, 2026-08-22. Continuation of the item-6a grep-first partial pass. Eight parallel research agents (4 Brazil, 4 China) covered every remaining unwired-to-international candidate node identified by a fresh component measurement (Brazil 86 unwired-to-international of 99 total nodes, China 48 of 66, up from the smaller counts recorded at BRICS/G.3 because the 2026-08-20 Grok archive mint substantially grew both countries' node counts in the meantime). Every mint below was independently raw-verified against a live, currently-reachable primary source this session (several agents caught and discarded WebFetch fabricating plausible content for dead/blocked URLs, verifying instead via direct curl+pdftotext or a real browser session) — no corpus node description was trusted as a citable source by itself, per the item-6a correction to the G.3 "grep node descriptions" technique. 8 new international-standard nodes minted (Oslo Manual, WHO Rose Angina Questionnaire, WHO GSHS, UN World Population Prospects methodology, FAO World Programme for the Census of Agriculture, UN SEEA, IMF Monetary and Financial Statistics Manual and Compilation Guide 2016, WHO ICD-10), 26 new dependency edges (22 Brazil, 4 China), and 22 `_dropped` entries recording honest negatives, a documented denial (br-ibge-pof vs COICOP; br-stn-resultado-tesouro-nacional vs GFSM 2014; cn-mineral-resources-report vs UNFC), and several leads for a future round (a second China-CAEP SEEA-EEA-2012 citation outside the exact candidate scope; an MNR-UNECE UNFC bridging document blocked by a 403 rather than by lack of a relationship; a new cn-stats-law/cn-stats-law-impl-regs vs cn-statistics-law duplicate-node finding, same shape as the br-ibge-sistema-contas-nacionais/br-scn duplicate flagged at item 6a). Brazil's industrial/business-statistics survey family (PIM-PF, PIA-Empresa, PIA-Produto, PAS, PAC, PAIC, PMC, PIMES, PINTEC) all connect to ISIC via IBGE/Concla's own CNAE concordance documentation, with PINTEC additionally connecting to the Oslo Manual and citing the Frascati Manual — the single richest node in the round.

reports.title: Oslo Manual
reports.description: International standard guidelines for collecting and interpreting data on business innovation activity, jointly published by the OECD and Eurostat as part of the Frascati Family of manuals. OECD's own page states: "The Oslo Manual is the foremost international source of guidelines for the collection and use of data on innovation activities in industry." Brazil's IBGE cites the 3rd edition (2005) by name in the technical notes of its own innovation survey, PINTEC: "A referência conceitual e metodológica da PINTEC é baseada na terceira edição do Manual de Oslo (OSLO..., 2005)."

reports.title: Rose Angina Questionnaire (WHO)
reports.description: A standardized angina-symptom screening instrument, first published by Geoffrey Rose in the WHO's own journal and subsequently recommended by WHO as a general population-survey tool, internationally known as the "WHO/Rose angina questionnaire." Original citation: Rose GA, "The diagnosis of ischaemic heart pain and intermittent claudication in field surveys," Bulletin of the World Health Organization, v.27, n.6, p.645-658, 1962.

reports.title: Global School-based Student Health Survey (GSHS)
reports.description: WHO's collaborative surveillance methodology and standardized questionnaire for measuring youth health behaviours. WHO's own page states: "The Global school-based student health survey (GSHS) is a collaborative surveillance project designed to help countries measure and assess the behavioural risk factors and protective factors in 10 key areas among young people aged 13 to 17 years."

reports.title: World Population Prospects — Methodology
reports.publisher: United Nations, Department of Economic and Social Affairs, Population Division
reports.description: The UN Population Division's methodology for its global population estimates and projections series, "World Population Prospects" (WPP) — covering fertility age-patterns, mortality model life tables, and migration methods used to produce official population estimates and projections for every UN member state. Brazil's IBGE names four distinct WPP/UN Population Division methodological choices directly in its own population-projection report: the WPP2024 fertility age-pattern, the UN(2015) old-age mortality adjustment expanding Wilmoth et al. (2012), the UN(2011) West Model Life Tables, and UN Manual VI (1970) for internal migration.

reports.title: World Programme for the Census of Agriculture (WCA)
reports.publisher: Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations (FAO)
reports.description: FAO's decadal international programme (running since 1950) establishing recommended concepts, definitions and methodology for national agricultural censuses, so results are internationally comparable. IBGE's own English-language page for its 2017 Census of Agriculture states: "the Institute used premises from the Programa del Censo Agropecuario Mundial 2020 (World Programme for the Census of Agriculture), implemented by the United Nations Organization and the Food and Agriculture Organization (FAO)... The results of the 2017 Census of Agriculture, as of those of previous editions, are in accordance with the recommendations and the basic concepts adopted by FAO."

reports.title: System of Environmental-Economic Accounting (SEEA)
reports.publisher: United Nations Statistics Division / UN Committee of Experts on Environmental-Economic Accounting
reports.description: UN international statistical standard framework for compiling environmental-economic accounts, comprising the SEEA Central Framework (2012), SEEA Experimental Ecosystem Accounting / SEEA-EEA (2012), its 2021 successor SEEA Ecosystem Accounting (SEEA-EA), and SEEA-Water. IBGE's own methodology page for its environmental-economic accounts states: "A metodologia da contabilidade econômica e ambiental vem sendo estabelecida pelas Nações Unidas por meio do Sistema de Contas Econômicas Ambientais - SCEA (System of Environmental-Economic Accounting - SEEA)," naming SEEA-EEA 2012 and SEEA-Water specifically for its ecosystem and water accounts.

reports.title: Monetary and Financial Statistics Manual and Compilation Guide (2016)
reports.description: The IMF's 2016 manual (successor to the 2000 Monetary and Financial Statistics Manual) setting the international methodological standard for compiling monetary and financial statistics — the monetary base, monetary aggregates, and the monetary-authority survey of assets and liabilities. Brazil's Banco Central do Brasil describes it, in its own words, as "referência metodológica de melhores práticas para a produção de estatísticas monetárias e financeiras" (methodological reference of best practices for producing monetary and financial statistics), citing "o padrão definido no Manual de Estatísticas Monetárias e Financeiras e Guia de Compilação (MEMF), edição 2016, do Fundo Monetário Internacional (FMI)" for its "crédito ampliado" statistic.

reports.title: International Statistical Classification of Diseases and Related Health Problems, 10th Revision (ICD-10)
reports.description: WHO's international standard diagnostic classification for epidemiology, health management and cause-of-death/morbidity statistics, adopted by the World Health Assembly in 1990 and in effect for member states from 1993 (superseded internationally by ICD-11, effective 2022, though ICD-10 remains in wide concurrent use). China's National Health Commission states in its own China Health Statistical Yearbook: "2000 年采用 ICD-9 国际疾病分类统计标准。2002 年起，采用 ICD-10 国际疾病分类统计标准。" ("In 2000, the ICD-9 international disease-classification statistical standard was adopted; from 2002 onward, the ICD-10 international disease-classification statistical standard has been used.")
